name: Maxakali Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language (Stoianov 2016/2017 cover handshape phonology only); word stress not applicable/undescribed

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page maxa1248 and reference records 553653, 553544
sources.note: Bibliography only: exactly two descriptive references (Stoianov 2016 MA; Stoianov & Nevins 2017), comment 'independent origin'. No other descriptions listed.

sources.citation: Stoianov, Diane & Andrew Nevins. 2017. The phonology of handshape distribution in Maxakalí sign. In Geoff Lindsey & Andrew Nevins (eds.), Sonic Signatures: Studies dedicated to John Harris (Language Faculty and Beyond 14), 232-262. Amsterdam/Philadelphia: John Benjamins. doi:10.1075/lfab.14.c14 (publisher 4th proofs posted as lingbuzz/004089, 2018)
sources.note: Nothing. The chapter analyses handshape inventory, markedness/complexity (Ann 2006, Brentari 2003 models), dispersion, and the non-dominant hand in Maxakalí sign; grep for stress/accent/prominence/rhythm/intonation returns 0 hits; 'prosodic' occurs only in references to Brentari's (1998) Prosodic Model and a generic Nespor & Vogel footnote. No statement on prominence, movement stress or prosody of Maxakalí sign.

sources.citation: Stoianov, Diane. 2016. Phonological Dispersion in Maxakalí Sign. MA thesis, University College London, 41 pp.

sources.note: The only other descriptive work on Maxakalí sign (Glottolog 553653); would confirm whether any movement/prosody observations exist beyond handshape, though title and hhtype 'minimal' suggest handshape dispersion only.

sources.note: Only the 2017 handshape chapter concerns Maxakalí sign; other Stoianov/Nevins sign-language papers (2022 Languages; 2023 Sign Language Studies; 2025 LFAB 20) concern Cena (a different Brazilian village sign language), not Maxakalí sign.
